passages.text:
Agrippina Minor, fīlia Germanicī et mater Nerōnis imperātōris, erat fēmina magnae potentiae. Multōs annōs, [underline: marītō suō Claudiō imperante], rem pūblicam summā cūrā administrābat. Multī senatōrēs eam timēbant, quod et Claudium imperātōrem et ipsum Nerōnem magnā cum arte regēbat. Saepe enim in cōnsiliīs aderat et prō salūte reī pūblicae loquī nōn timēbat. Quam ob rem nōmen eius per tōtam Italiam clārum erat.

Nerō autem, postquam imperātor factus est, mātrem suam pati nōluit. Tandem nūntiōs suōs mīsit quī Agrippinam interficerent. Quod ubi audīvit, Agrippina, [underline: nūntiīs mortem suam portantibus] respondēns, pectus suum aperuit et “hūc fērī!” inquit.

Post mortem eius, fāma sceleris Nerōnis per tōtam Italiam vulgāta est. Multī Rōmānī crēdēbant eum tyrannum esse. Ita Agrippina, quamquam cum magnā virtūte vīxerat, per vim fīliī suī occīsa est. Memoria tamen eius apud multōs Rōmānōs diū manēbat.

What is the best translation of Multōs annōs, marītō suō Claudiō imperante, rem pūblicam summā cūrā administrābat?
options: She administered public affairs with great care for many years, while her husband Claudius was ruling.
For many years after her husband Claudius ruled, she managed public affairs with great care.
She and her husband Claudius jointly administered public affairs with great care for many years.
Her husband Claudius administered public affairs with great care for many years.

questions.prompt: What is the best translation of Tandem nūntiōs suōs mīsit quī Agrippinam interficerent?
options: Finally, he sent his messengers who had killed Agrippina.
He finally sent his messengers to kill Agrippina.
At last, Agrippina sent her messengers who were to be killed.
His messengers, who had come to kill him, were finally sent away.

options: Many Romans were believed to be tyrants by him.

questions.prompt: According to the passage, why did many senators fear Agrippina?
options: She had exiled them from Rome.
She governed both Emperor Claudius and Nero himself with great skill.
She had poisoned her husband Claudius.
She had led an army against them.

questions.prompt: According to the passage, what did Agrippina do when she heard Nero's plan?
options: She fled to the temple for sanctuary.
She sent her own messengers to negotiate with Nero.
She exposed her chest and said 'Strike here!'
She appealed to the senate for protection.

questions.prompt: What does the passage say about Nero's reputation after Agrippina's death?
options: He was celebrated as a wise ruler throughout Italy.
News of his crime spread throughout all Italy.
The senate voted to honor him for his decision.
He was mourned by all Romans as a tragic figure.

options: Most Romans approved of Nero's decision as politically necessary.
Nero's reputation was damaged and Romans viewed the act as criminal.
Romans were indifferent to Agrippina's death since she had too much power.

questions.prompt: What is the best translation of Nerō autem, postquam imperātor factus est, mātrem suam patī nōluit?
options: But Nero, after he became emperor, was unwilling to tolerate his mother.
But Nero, before he became emperor, had refused to listen to his mother.
Nero became emperor because his mother would no longer tolerate him.
After his mother refused him, Nero was made emperor against his will.

questions.prompt: According to the passage, what does the phrase nōmen eius per tōtam Italiam clārum erat tell us about Agrippina?
options: Her name was feared only within the city of Rome.
Her reputation was famous throughout all Italy.
Her name appeared in official Roman state records.
She was known throughout Italy solely as a devoted wife.
